records.question: What was the primary purpose of this document?
records.ground_truth_answer: To provide local and federal partners with baseline information and survey methods to allow for continued monitoring efforts to evaluate the effectiveness of management actions taken at the Samoa Maritime quarry in Fagaʻalu, American Samoa.
ground_truth_chunks: The primary purpose of this document is to provide local and federal partners with baseline information and survey methods to allow for continued monitoring efforts to evaluate the effectiveness of management actions taken at the Samoa Maritime quarry in Fagaʻalu, American Samoa.

This document summarizes work completed between 2012 and 2014, and was coordinated and funded by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Coral Reef Conservation Program (CRCP) to gather baseline data and information before management interventions such as drainage systems, alternative ground cover, and retention ponds were installed at the quarry to reduce land-based sources of pollution inputs to the coral reefs in Fagaʻalu Bay.

records.question: What mitigation measure was installed in August 2012 to intercept groundwater flow at the Samoa Maritime quarry?
records.ground_truth_answer: In August 2012, groundwater drainage diversions were installed at two locations to intercept clean groundwater flow: immediately below the exposed rock face at the Excavation Area and between the Excavation Platform and Upper Operational Area.
ground_truth_chunks: Prior to intervention, perennial groundwater flows were discharged from a spring in the quarry blast face and flowed over the haul roads, Excavation Platform, and Operational Areas of the quarry, eroding sediment into the stream and elevating suspended sediment concentration (SSC) during non-storm conditions. In August 2012, groundwater drainage diversions to intercept clean groundwater flow were installed at two locations: a) immediately below the exposed rock face at the Excavation Area, and b) between the Excavation Platform and Upper Operational Area (dotted blue lines, **[Figure 3](#page-9-0)**).
